[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"C# Operators: Arithmetic, Logical, and Bitwise"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Operators are symbols that instruct the compiler to perform specific mathematical or logical manipulations. C# provides a rich set of operators to perform various operations. This tutorial covers arithmetic, logical, and bitwise operators."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Arithmetic Operators"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Arithmetic operators perform mathematical calculations. The following table lists the arithmetic operators available in C#:"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"+ (Addition): Adds two operands. Example: x + y"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"- (Subtraction): Subtracts the second operand from the first. Example: x - y"},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"* (Multiplication): Multiplies two operands. Example: x * y"},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"/ (Division): Divides the first operand by the second. Example: x / y"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"% (Modulus): Returns the remainder of the division. Example: x % y"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"++ (Increment): Increases the value of the operand by 1. Example: x++ (post-increment), ++x (pre-increment)"},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"-- (Decrement): Decreases the value of the operand by 1. Example: x-- (post-decrement), --x (pre-decrement)"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"int x = 10;
int y = 5;

Console.WriteLine("x + y = " + (x + y)); // Output: x + y = 15
Console.WriteLine("x - y = " + (x - y)); // Output: x - y = 5
Console.WriteLine("x * y = " + (x * y)); // Output: x * y = 50
Console.WriteLine("x / y = " + (x / y)); // Output: x / y = 2
Console.WriteLine("x % y = " + (x % y)); // Output: x % y = 0

x++;
Console.WriteLine("x++ = " + x); // Output: x++ = 11

y--;
Console.WriteLine("y-- = " + y); // Output: y-- = 4"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Logical Operators"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Logical operators are used to combine or modify boolean expressions. The following table lists the logical operators available in C#:"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"&& (Logical AND): Returns true if both operands are true. Example: x && y"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"|| (Logical OR): Returns true if at least one operand is true. Example: x || y"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"! (Logical NOT): Reverses the logical state of its operand. Example: !x"},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"bool x = true;
bool y = false;

Console.WriteLine("x && y = " + (x && y)); // Output: x && y = False
Console.WriteLine("x || y = " + (x || y)); // Output: x || y = True
Console.WriteLine("!x = " + (!x));   // Output: !x = False"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Bitwise Operators"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Bitwise operators perform operations on individual bits of integers. The following table lists the bitwise operators available in C#:"},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"& (Bitwise AND): Performs a bitwise AND operation. Example: x & y"},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"| (Bitwise OR): Performs a bitwise OR operation. Example: x | y"},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"^ (Bitwise XOR): Performs a bitwise XOR (exclusive OR) operation. Example: x ^ y"},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"~ (Bitwise NOT): Performs a bitwise NOT (one's complement) operation. Example: ~x"},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"<< (Left Shift): Shifts the bits of the first operand to the left by the number of positions specified by the second operand. Example: x << y"},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":">> (Right Shift): Shifts the bits of the first operand to the right by the number of positions specified by the second operand. Example: x >> y"},{"order":27,"type":"code","text":"int x = 5;  // Binary: 0101
int y = 3;  // Binary: 0011

Console.WriteLine("x & y = " + (x & y)); // Output: x & y = 1 (Binary: 0001)
Console.WriteLine("x | y = " + (x | y)); // Output: x | y = 7 (Binary: 0111)
Console.WriteLine("x ^ y = " + (x ^ y)); // Output: x ^ y = 6 (Binary: 0110)
Console.WriteLine("~x = " + (~x));   // Output: ~x = -6 (Binary: 111...1010 - two's complement)
Console.WriteLine("x << 1 = " + (x << 1)); // Output: x << 1 = 10 (Binary: 1010)
Console.WriteLine("x >> 1 = " + (x >> 1)); // Output: x >> 1 = 2 (Binary: 0010)"}]
